head: Two stick insects new to science turned up in Australia, one hiding in plain sight for decades.
summary: Researchers writing in Austral Entomology on September 21 described Anchiale mabiensis, whose lidded eggs carry concentric rings unlike any recorded in stick insects, and Anchiale robusta, misidentified for decades. They also reinstated Anchiale albopunctata, mistaken for another species for more than a century, and females of mabiensis reach 6.4 inches. Braxton Jones of the University of Sydney said even among Australia's most photographed insects, species are still escaping recognition.
